newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-WOMEN'S STANDINGS AFTER FINAL SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WOMEN'S STANDINGS AFTER FINAL SLALOM.

text.p: Following are brief
profiles of the co-winners of the World Cup women's slalom at
the World Cup Finals on Sunday:
Name: Pernilla Wiberg
Age: 26
Nationality: Swedish
World Cup wins: 21; 14 slaloms, 1 giant slalom, 3 Super-G, 1
downhill, 2 combined
Wiberg, winner of four slalom and two Super-G races entering
the World Cup Finals this season, had already clinched the
overall championship, becoming the first Scandinavian woman to
win the crown. She captured her first career downhill at the
Finals to become the only active woman skier to own wins in
all four World Cup disciplines. Wiberg won Olympic gold in
1992 in the giant slalom and in 1994 in the combined. She won
world championship gold in the giant slalom in 1991 and the
1996 world title in combined.
Name: Lara Magoni
Age: 28
Nationality: Italian
World Cup wins: 1
Other feats: Won first World Cup race in season finale at
Vail. Took silver medal in the slalom at the world
championships at Sestriere. Finished second the week before
the Sestriere championships at Laax. A late bloomer who joined
the World Cup circuit in 1991.
